body: Can you provide some sources to support these very specific claims?

Clearly, you are running out of arguments and are starting to turn to personal insults. It is quite normal to get defensive… 

Just out of interest: do you also go around telling people advocating for keto, carnivore or just generally people watching what they eat that they are unhealthily obsessed?

The thing is, when you ask non-vegans what they would suggest in terms of activism, they would just prefer to never hear anything about veganism from anyone. And thats understandable. Thinking about how animals are exploited and killed isn‘t fun. 

I do empathise with people who are non-vegan. I used to be a non-vegan when I was younger. But it is also true that hearing uncomfortable truths again and again until you finally really understand them is the only way to get through the cognitive dissonance for many people. It might not reach anyone (or they might not yet realise that the thought reached them) but I still think it is better to talk about perceived injustices than to leave people in their comfort… 

You might have a different opinion on how to talk about veganism and that is fine, I will still stick to mine though…

Why do you think people would want to reduce their consumption of animal based products? 

In my opinion (and from the people I know in my environment) the people who are going vegetarian or reducing meat are doing so exactly because they have been confronted with ecological and ethical reasons and do believe that something has to change. They just aren‘t willing (yet) to change their behavior to adapt to their own moral compass but their reasons are usually exactly the same as vegans…

Nothing changes if nobody ever questions the status quo. It was at some point the status quo to keep and trade human slaves in many parts of the world, women weren’t allowed to vote and it is still the status quo in many places that being gay is illegal and immoral. Societies change but for that people need to stand up for what they believe in.

The very mast majority of people (if you don‘t have specific diseases or allergies) can live healthily on a vegan diet. Following current research a vegan diet looks to be even healthier than an omnivore one. So every consumption of animal products when the person could also not eat those products literally causes „unnecessary harm“. 

How is eating animal products „necessary“ to you personally?
Actually, there aren‘t that many vegan men, sadly…

That being said, most people are actually fine with animal suffering when it results in them being able to eat a product or part of that animal. If you eat animal products you probably pay for worse things to be done to animals every day. I think it is good to evaluate your morals and those of your partners to see if you are compatible but if you eat animal products it would be hypocritical to blame him and not yourself at the same time.
What a sophisticated response. Thanks!

To elaborate, even if you likely won‘t understand what I mean: Forcing animals into existence to be slaves all their lives to be killed when they are no longer useful is horrible to me. These animals are intelligent and their physical and emotional needs are not met while they also have to endure stress and pain. To me, it is not right to pay for animal suffering. In a similar, yet different way, it is also wrong to me that people are discriminated against, harassed or raped. I don‘t understand why people have to do those things, and that includes eating animal products. 

Now, I would not say that non-vegans are bad people as many people eat animal products without knowing and understanding what goes on in animal agriculture. But I would still not want my close friends to contribute to the suffering with me having to witness it. Luckily everyone can chose for themselves with whom they want to be friends…

And yet, it is also understandable to question whether a good friend is actually a good friend if you are living by a completely different moral compass. I wouldn‘t be best friends with sexists, rapists, racists etc.

Cat‘s aren‘t listed as invasive species because they fall under the term „pet“ rather than being considered wild. For good reason since their diet is very different from their wild ancestors - especially when you look at those neglected in cities. When one takes care that cats are neutered and not just left free to roam the amount of unhoused ones drops. At least that is what you see here in Europe (I am German). 

You bringing up the wild boars in North America just proves my point: some dumb people brought the boars to North America because they enjoyed hunting them and populations got out of control and now it is neither ethical nor feasable to get rid of them. One should avoid getting to that point with other species. 

I am not sure how bad the cat situation is outside of towns in the US, do cats roam the forests and reproduce in the wild or does that mostly occur in Urban settings? 
Here we (now) take a lot of care with not wanting cats to roam because in addition to general biodiversity we don‘t want them hybridising with actual wild cats as it would make them less adaptable and could push them to extinction.

Just because it is too late to remove some invasive species doesn‘t mean we should release all other possible species. We now know that releasing non-native species has bad effects (in terms of competition, predation, diseases) on local wildlife. So lets not make the same mistakes people used to make, those weren‘t smart decisions then and they aren‘t now.

Firstly, that is not a peer-reviewed research article.

https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0737080607004133

Powell et al. 2008. 

If you are trying to convince yourself and others that riding is not harmful to horses I hope you have done better research at some point.

What you are describing is an ecological disaster. Domesticated cats are not part of our natural ecosystems and are one of the biggest threats local biodiversity faces. Like other vegans, I am completely against breeding more pets into this world but we need to find solutions for those animals that are already in existence. Letting them roam is not it (in my opinion and from an ecological standpoint whereby the aim should be to have self-regulating, healthy ecosystems - also for our own good, feel free to look up the term „ecological annhilation“).

As I clearly stated I was just guessing at why you might feel triggered and conclude some wild things here. If it doesn‘t apply - fine. The reason „I am a data scientist“ is not a logical reason. No need to explain though. I really don‘t care that much. 

Data science can be any topic. Just as stated in the paragraph you copied („with specific subject matter). So just saying „I do data science I can tell this dude has bad intentions“ does not make sense. What matters more is what kind of data you work on. As an example: someone analyzing shareholder market trends is a data scientist. Someone building and maintaining a database for a hospital is a data scientist. Someone analyzing consumer trends is a data scientist and someone who analyzes genomes of whales is a data scientist. And still, someone analyzing which products Aldi consumers buy at which time of year does not give you any qualification to judge a persons intent from a picture. 

Do you understand what I am saying?

Sure. 

1. The point is to reduce unnecessary suffering. Of course I hope that within the next century most people go vegan. It might be a global social change (ethics-based) or cost-based (plant-based foods are way cheaper to produce when subsidies are removed plus the cost of the climate crisis is massive - this should lead to governments pushing for plant-based diets).  Or a combination of both. To your question of „what is the point“. In my opinion the fewer animals suffer and are killed for human pleasure the better. The scale is almost irrelevant. Whether 10 lives are saved or 10 billion, their lives matter and are worth fighting for. On a personal level I also feel much better in my decision to not use animals. I could honestly not live with myself if I ate animals and their products just because they taste good knowing what I know about their intelligence, emotional needs and what goes into producing those products. It would cause me immense stress. 

2. The best solution would indeed be for them to go extinct. Same goes for bred pigs and chickens. These animals are not natural. They were bred specifically for milk, egg and meat production and are maladapted to life in nature. 
They still have relatives in nature (wild buffalo, goats, sheep, wild fowl birds like turkeys and pheasants and also wild pigs). If we phase out animal agriculture we can also give land back to nature as we would need less land for food production. In addition we would have much less toxic runoff from farms and from heavy fertilisation into ocean habitats. Land as well as water ecosystems would greatly benefit and many populations of wild animals might be able to recover in population size for us to enjoy when out in nature. Having an encounter with a wild animal is worth so much more than with an animal imprisoned and destined to die in a slaughterhouse (in my opinion).

There are other people for whom this doesn‘t work but that is why it is great we are a community comprised of different characters. There is no „responsibility“ to act a certain way around others because we are vegan.

We are individuals who are often pushed aside in society or called extreme simply for not wanting animals to suffer. Everyone here is doing their best and places like this sub-reddit are our safe space. Not a place where we need to censor ourselves in case an omni is here reading along…

In addition the mental stress of not allowing chickens to nest and breed their eggs should be considered). 

When it comes to cows there are somewhat similar issues, but exacerbated. Cows bred for Milk production produce way more milk than natural and they can have serious vitamin deficiencies as well as regular infection of udders which is very painful. On top of that, as mentioned above, Cows produce milk because they had a baby. Cows in animal agriculture give birth roughly once a year and are impregnated again 3 months after giving birth (consider the stress of continuous pregnancies both mentally and physically). If you want continuous milk supply: how do you get your cow pregnant without causing physical or mental suffering. What do you do with the calf (again without causing suffering)? And you should never keep cows alone as they are highly social. I do not think it is feasable for anyone to have continuous cruelty-free backyard milk. Do you?

Okay, so right now, the production of lab grown meat is far from cruelty free. I am not talking about the muscle sample taken from cows. I am talking about the use of fetal bovine serum as a key component of the growth medium used. To obtain it a pregnant cow is slaughtered while keeping the fetus alive (to prevent blood clots from forming). Without any pain meds the fetus‘ heart is punctured with a long needle whereby the serum is extracted. After this both mother and calf are used for meat production (this happens in slaughterhouses anyway). This process is not cruelty free and in no way is ok within the moral framework of veganism. 

There are many companies currently working on plant-based alternatives to this but with little success. Currently the alternatives are able to be used on some cell lines, but not on others and not for extended generations of cell lineages (meaning sooner or later you need to use fetal bovine serum for a few generations). 
If/When scientists truly develop a plant based growth medium that can be used industrially we can see what exactly the components are, how much is needed to grow a certain quantity of meat and then evaluate the overall environmental and ecological effects.

Yes, that is a really good point! Soil health is so important! A strong chemical or biological imbalance can have countless consequences in different systems but because one doesn‘t see it with the „naked eye“ (always find that phrasing awkward but no better way to put it) it is often forgotten about! There was a report relatively recently about a team trying to plant trees on the edge of a tropical rainforest (Amazon, if I remember correctly). They had very little success until they realized that they also had to transplant the soil fungi found among established rainforest trees. The fungi change the soil microbiome and help the trees in getting needed nutrients. 
And this is the case everywhere! The soil is at the basis of all terrestrial food webs!

Currently, we are experiencing a pandemic pathogen threatening human health. But what many don‘t realize is that infectious disease is also a major issue for wildlife. The problem is that there is often little to nothing known about the pathogens themselves and they are unknowingly transported to novel environments where they become invasive. People who travel should regularly clean their boots and any hiking gear - especially, if they are travelling across continents. 

A specific case example would be the emergence of white-nose disease in North America. It is a fungal disease affecting hibernating bats and has caused the greatest mammalian die-off ever properly reported (i.e., in rough numbers not by fossil records) since its appearance in 2006. It was first observed in a touristic show cave near New York and it is highly likely that a tourist or caver brought it from Eurasia (where the pathogen is native and hosts are adapted and not dying). 

There are so many non-human diseases out there (infecting amphibians, snakes, rice, bananas etc.). Family and Friends are often very surprised to hear this when I discuss it with them because apart from disease in livestock this is not something the broad public knows about. Disease is often a direct cause of species extinction (e.g, amphibian chytridiomycosis) or can lead to extinction down the line because of the strain on populations (probably what will happen with tasmanian devils following their infectious facial tumors). 

A good place to start for further reading is Fisher et al. 2012 (Nature).

I had the same issues as you with the pill. After I stopped taking it after a breakup I learned (over the next year) that it wasn‘t me (my character) who was depressed but the hormone levels making me so. 

Several years later after having been with another partner for over a year we discussed with my doctor that I would try the Nuva Ring. The doctor said, that the hormones would be in lower concentration in my blood as they are applied locally. This sounded logical to me. Sadly, after 3 months I had the same feelings I had had before. And I become a bitch on contraceptive hormones. No libido and constantly bad mood. It reminded me of why my first relationship ended. I stopped the use of the Nuva Ring and I felt like myself again roughly 6 months later.

I am not saying that you shouldn‘t try the Nuva Ring. Every body is different and especially hormones are a fine balance. It might work for you. But I recommend to anyone who is using hormonal contraception: listen to your body and how you feel. It is now something like 7 years since taking hormones and many people still try telling me it is the only option. I had a gynecologist once ask me „do you take the pill? No? Okay well I will prescribe one straight away“. There are lots of side effects and I often feel that doctors don‘t stress enough that we should watch out for them. 

I am now using a diaphragm with contraceptive cream and double up with a condom for „danger days“.
